title: Interactive Derivation Canvas Demo
description: A short recording-ready sequence of handwritten derivations that ramps from algebra to physics and keeps a running score.

blocks.title: Derivation sprint
blocks.content_html:
Four handwritten challenges build into one clean physics result. Each canvas reads your lines, marks valid equations, and adds points when you reach the target.

The sequence starts with a one-line algebra move, then isolates a square-root quantity, then derives a spring launch speed, then finishes with the loop-the-loop threshold.

blocks.title: Calibrate the canvas
blocks.prompt: Start from the calibration equation and isolate x.
hints: Undo the +3 by subtracting 3 from both sides.

blocks.title: Unlock a square root
blocks.prompt: A later physics problem will need speed from energy. Solve the kinetic-energy equation for v.
hints: Divide by m so v^2 is alone.
Use the positive square root for speed.

blocks.title: Spring launch speed
blocks.prompt: Now use the same square-root move to derive the launch speed from a compressed spring.
hints: Cancel the 1/2 on both sides first.
Divide by m to isolate v^2.
Take the positive square root. Since A is an amplitude, use A > 0.

blocks.title: Loop-the-loop threshold
blocks.prompt: Finish with the classic loop threshold. At the top of the loop, gravity supplies the centripetal force: mg = m v^2 / R. Energy from height h becomes kinetic energy plus height 2R at the top. Derive the minimum h.
valid_forms: \frac{1}{2} m v^2 + m g (2R) = m g h
hints: Use the force equation first to get v^2 = gR.
At the top, the ball is at height 2R, so its potential energy is mg(2R).
Substitute v^2 = gR, then cancel m and g.
